name: KMIGT Grand Island and Nebraska Ethanol Expansion

values.SegmentName: Grand Island and Nebraska Ethanol Expansion
values.Owner: Kinder Morgan Interstate Gas Transmission LLC

researcher_notes: A Federal Energy Regulatory Commission notice from January 2008 (docket CP08-44, blanket authorization request) describes two mainline loops: about 7.5 miles of 16-inch pipe and about 17 miles of 12-inch pipe in Hall, Merrick and Nance counties, Nebraska, to serve five ethanol shippers under binding agreements for 21,810 Dth per day, at an estimated cost of 23,940,143 dollars. Total new pipe is 24.5 miles, about 39 km, above the 25 km add threshold. The EIA August 2026 release (Historical Projects sheet, Excel row 585, KM Nebraska Ethanol Expansion Project, 24.5 miles, 12 and 16 inch, docket CP08-44) lists it as completed in January 2009. Excel row 550 (KM 2008 Grand Island Expansion, completed November 2008) is the same project. Both EIA entries trace to one EIA release, and the FERC notice is a separate origin. A Natural Gas Intelligence article from 2008 reports the Grand Island extension at 25,000 Dth per day, which differs slightly from the 21,810 filed; filed figure used. Recorded as a new expansion row under the parent system P0208 (Tallgrass Interstate Gas Transmission, formerly Kinder Morgan Interstate Gas Transmission, sold in 2014); no existing row covers it. The sponsor name in the filings is Kinder Morgan Interstate Gas Transmission LLC; entity lookup found no exact match, so the owner is spelled as the source gives it and the ownership team should set the current owner. Start and end points are not stated beyond the counties; no route was found. The ownership change to Tallgrass is from general knowledge and not sourced here.
